physics_note: Physics estimate, not data and not a trained model. Buoyant velocity u_b = √(g·β·ΔT·L) with β = 1/T_air (ideal gas); Richardson number Ri = (u_b/u)² compares buoyancy with the fan-driven air speed u. Ri ≫ 1: buoyancy feeds the flame; Ri ≪ 1: the fans do; in orbit Ri ≈ 0 and only the fans (or diffusion) bring fresh air. The 0.1-10 band for 'mixed' is a common rule of thumb.
smoke_note: Physics estimate, not data. Smoke is carried at roughly the larger of the fan air speed and the buoyant plume speed √(g·β·ΔT·L) (combined here as √(u_fan² + u_b²)); delay = distance ÷ that speed. It ignores mixing, dilution and the detector's own response time, so real delays are longer. In orbit with the fans off only slow diffusion remains.
